chunks: As for what Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr narrated — he said: it was narrated to me from 'Abdullah, meaning Ibn al-Mughira, who elevates it to Abu 'Abdillah, peace be upon him:
that the kurr is six hundred ratls.

The first thing regarding it is that it is mursal (disconnected), not musnad (properly chained). Furthermore, it contradicts the hadiths we have narrated. And beyond that, none of our jurists have acted upon it.

It is also possible that the one who asked about the kurr was from a region whose customary ratl weighs the equivalent of two Baghdad ratls, and so he [the Imam] gave a fatwa according to what he knew of their custom — thus making it encompass the quantity we have established for the kurr.
Then the Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — said: Running water is not made impure by that [impurity], whether it is little or much. And that which indicates this [follows]…

key_terms.الرِّطْلُ: ratl — a unit of weight varying by region; the Baghdad ratl was the juristic standard reference
key_terms.الْكُرُّ: kurr — the minimum volume of still water that resists ritual impurity on contact with najasah
key_terms.الْمَاءُ الْجَارِي: running/flowing water — a distinct fiqh category not rendered impure regardless of quantity
key_terms.مُرْسَلٌ: mursal — a hadith with a broken chain; a narrator between Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Ibn al-Mughira is missing
key_terms.مُسْنَدٍ: musnad — a hadith with an unbroken, fully attributed chain back to its source

ai.seo_question: What did Shaykh al-Tusi say about the narration that a kurr equals 600 ratls in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This passage from Tahdhib al-Ahkam presents and critiques a mursal (disconnected) narration transmitted via Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, elevated to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), claiming a kurr of water equals 600 ratls. Shaykh al-Tusi rejects it as disconnected, contradictory to established narrations, and unacted upon by jurists; he offers a possible reconciliation through regional weight differences (whereby 600 local ratls equal 1200 Baghdad ratls), then cites Shaykh al-Mufid's ruling that flowing water is never rendered impure regardless of quantity.
